title: Ninety Days to a Ceasefire
thesis: The path from the March strikes on Iran to a Geneva peace framework compressed into a single season, proving the bombing and the back-channel were one policy run on two clocks.
body:
The path from open war to a signed framework took barely a season. What looked in March like the opening of a years-long campaign instead collapsed into a negotiated pause by June — an arc compressed by exhaustion on every side [sy_332fe335b7a7, sy_0b4cd1d8d0cd].

<timeline emphasis="escalation">
<step date="2026-03-09">US aircraft strike Iranian missile-production sites, and Tehran vows a calibrated response [sy_332fe335b7a7].</step>
<step date="2026-04-22">Qatar quietly opens a back-channel, carrying messages between Washington and Tehran [sy_3ea3e1ab1e4b].</step>
<step date="2026-05-30">Negotiators initial a preliminary peace framework in Geneva [sy_a9392e00ca9a]. [qt_d9cff62941ba]</step>
<step date="2026-06-11">An Israel-Hezbollah truce holds, removing the last live front [sy_0b4cd1d8d0cd].</step>
</timeline>

<stat value="90 days" label="from the first March strikes to the Geneva framework">the entire arc, start to finish [sy_332fe335b7a7, sy_a9392e00ca9a]</stat>

<callout>The lesson of the ninety days is that the strikes and the back-channel were never contradictory — they were the same policy, run on two clocks [sy_332fe335b7a7, sy_3ea3e1ab1e4b]</callout>

What remains is durability. A framework initialed under battlefield pressure is not a treaty, and the actors who signed it each read the same document as a different kind of victory [sy_a9392e00ca9a, sy_0b4cd1d8d0cd].
